key_insight: Constitutive-Set Mechanics replaces a single material law with all experimentally admissible laws and uses variational mechanics to certify robust structural response from the states a structure actually visits.
engineering_relevance: This enables safer design under constitutive uncertainty by bounding worst-case performance without assuming one definitive material model.
method: Formulate the constitutive uncertainty as an admissible set and evaluate it through a support function of the occupation measure.
Use the structural equilibrium solve to generate robust energy certificates; global minimization gives two-sided bounds.
Apply the framework to elasticity, fracture, shells, and membrane tests to infer and bound response under incomplete material data.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports demonstrations on multiple problems, including a shell where only 4 of 226 constitutive directions are interrogated and a membrane where the certified worst-case energy is more than four times the reference.
watch_item: The approach depends on accurate definition of the admissible constitutive set, so results can be sensitive to how experimental constraints and uncertainty bounds are specified.
paper_title: Constitutive-Set Mechanics: variational mechanics on an admissible set of constitutive laws
